subject: Maths
subtopic: Division as the inverse of multiplication
title: Division as the inverse of multiplication
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (2, 5, 10 Times Tables) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can use multiplication facts to solve division problems by recognising they are inverse operations.

key_vocab.definition: Inverse means opposite. Multiplication and division are inverses: one undoes the other.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can use multiplication facts to solve division problems by recognising they are inverse operations.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Inverse -- Inverse means opposite. Multiplication and division are inverses: one undoes the other.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
If a × b = c, then c ÷ a = b AND c ÷ b = a. Use what you know about times tables to divide.
7 × 8 = 56 → 56 ÷ 7 = 8
Same numbers, inverse operation

Key examples:
  ✓ 5 × 6 = 30  (multiplication)
  ✓ 6 × 5 = 30  (commutative)
  ✓ 30 ÷ 5 = 6  (inverse)
  ✓ 30 ÷ 6 = 5  (inverse)
  ✗ 30 ÷ 30 = 1 × 5 + 6  (doesn't follow)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – fact family from a multiplication
  If 4 × 7 = 28, write the four related facts.
  4 × 7 = 28
  7 × 4 = 28
  28 ÷ 4 = 7,  28 ÷ 7 = 4
  Four facts
  (Same three numbers (4, 7, 28) just rearranged.)

Example 2 – use multiplication to divide
  Calculate 42 ÷ 6
  Think: 6 × ___ = 42
  From times table: 6 × 7 = 42
  So 42 ÷ 6 = 7
  = 7
  (Recall the multiplication fact, then read off the inverse.)

sections.title: Check with the inverse
sections.content:
Is each statement correct? Use multiplication to check.

(a) 84 ÷ 7 = 12 — check by 7×12
(b) 54 ÷ 6 = 8 — check by 6×8
(c) 121 ÷ 11 = 11 — check
(d) 96 ÷ 8 = 11 — check

sections.title: Missing-number problems
sections.content:
Use the inverse to find the unknown.

(a) ___ ÷ 9 = 8
(b) 144 ÷ ___ = 12
(c) ___ ÷ 7 = 11
(d) 108 ÷ ___ = 9

sections.title: Mixed fact-family practice
sections.content:
Spot the multiplication fact you need.

(a) If 12 × 6 = 72, then 72 ÷ 6 = ___
(b) If 8 × 9 = 72, then 72 ÷ 9 = ___
(c) 11 × 11 = ___, so 121 ÷ 11 = ___
(d) If 7 × 5 = 35, then 35 ÷ 5 = ___
(e) Write 4 facts from 4 × 6 = 24

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Division is the inverse of multiplication
✓ If 7×9=63, then 63÷7=9
✗ Division is commutative: 12÷3 = 3÷12
✓ If a×b = c, then c÷a = b
✓ Multiplication undoes division
